title: Audit log exporter: private installer wiring, retention sinks, and Terraform module updates for Private deployments
author: Jordan Park
release_notes: Add support for wiring audit-log-exporter into Private installer and Terraform modules; configure per-customer retention sinks and optional per-tenant BigQuery/S3 exports. No breaking changes for existing hosted deployments.
description: Motivation: Private customers require automated wiring of audit-log-exporter as part of the Private/VPC installer so audit records are retained and exported according to compliance configs. This PR wires the exporter into the installer and Terraform modules, adds configurable retention sinks (S3, BigQuery) and retention TTLs, and updates Helm values and upgrade/rollback hooks to ensure safe rollouts. Changes included: installer wiring (private-installer templates + controller hooks); Helm chart updates for audit-log-exporter (values, pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks, pod disruption budgets); Terraform module changes to surface export sinks and IAM bindings; migration helper script that converts existing per-tenant retention settings into new sink objects; unit and integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Add installer templates and wiring for audit-log-exporter - [x] Add Helm values and lifecycle hooks for migration and safe rollback - [x] Expose retention_sinks and retention_ttl in Terraform module - [x] Add IAM binding helpers for BigQuery/S3 exporters (opt-in) - [x] Add e2e test harness using the perf-canary Private testbed - [x] Update docs and upgrade notes (redwood-docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/private/audit-logs) Migration notes: default behavior preserves existing retention_policy unless a retention_sinks entry is provided; migration helper is idempotent; enabling BigQuery/S3 exports requires customers to provide external destination credentials or use managed credentials via KMS integration. Rollout plan: staged canary in two Private testbeds, then opt-in rollouts for early-enterprise customers, then platform-wide rollout after 2-week stability window.

review_thread: Priya Singh (reviewer): Can you confirm the migration job is idempotent and safe to run across multiple upgrades?; Jordan Park (author): Yes, the migration script uses sink existence checks and a resource tag; it is safe to run multiple times and will noop if sinks exist.

Marco Alvarez (reviewer): The Terraform IAM module seems to require org-level privileges. Can we gate it behind a flag so customers opt-in?; Jordan Park (author): Agreed, added export_provider_enable flags and documented required privileges in the module README.

Leah Thompson (reviewer): Helm hooks can cause restarts during upgrade; what's the rollback story?; Jordan Park (author): Pre-upgrade job runs migration and writes a marker; post-upgrade checks ensure exporter is ready. On rollback, post-upgrade hook will not delete sinks; sinks are retained to avoid data loss. Added PDB to minimize disruption.

testing_notes: Ran e2e on two Private perf canaries and one customer staging deployment. Verified: sink objects created, sample events arrived in S3/BigQuery, migration helper idempotent, helm hooks behaved as expected under canary traffic. Observability: added smoke metric redwood.audit_exporter.sink_up with tagging by provider.
notes_for_operators: If customers opt-in to BigQuery exports, ensure service account has roles/bigquery.dataEditor and roles/storage.objectCreator if using GCS staging; for S3 ensure bucket policy allows PutObject by the exporter principal. To debug sink failures, check audit-exporter logs and pre-upgrade-job pod logs in the installer namespace.
